newsitem.title: USA: Boyfriend of accused Cosby extortionist charged.
newsitem.headline: Boyfriend of accused Cosby extortionist charged.

text.p: The boyfriend of the woman charged with trying to extort $40 million from entertainer Bill Cosby by claiming she is his illegitimate daughter pleaded guilty in the case on Tuesday and is cooperating with authorities, prosecutors said.
Antonay Williams, 26, of Perry, Fla., pleaded guilty in Manhattan federal court to one count each of conspiracy and aiding and abetting an extortion.

During the plea hearing, Williams identified himself as the boyfriend of Autumn Jackson, who is accused of trying to extort $40 million from Cosby by threatening to sell her story to a tabloid newspaper.
Jackson, 22, was released from federal prison on Monday on a $250,000 personal recognisance bond.

Williams told the court he helped Jackson and an accomplice Jose Medina in their scheme by threatening to disclose to the media that Cosby was her father. He said some of the threats were made through faxes and interstate phone calls.
He admitted charges that his involvement included doing research on Cosby, Cosby's corporate sponsors, and on the CBS television network that airs Cosby's programme.

The charges against Williams state that the defendants drafted letters to be sent to CBS to futher pressure Cosby to give Jackson money. An attachment to the CBS letter contained an unsigned agreement between Jackson, Medina and a "tabloid" in which the newspaper was to have paid money for the rights
During the plea hearing, Williams said he had received a document from a representative of the Globe tabloid.

He also admitted helping Jackson and Medina get to the Los Angeles airport on Jan. 17 to travel to a New York meeting with a Cosby representative who was to give them the cash and making return travel arrangements for them the following day.

"At first I was unaware that certain actions that I was asked to take were part of an extortion scheme; however, after it became apparent to me that the scheme involved an attempt to extort money from Mr. Cosby, I voluntarily continued to assist Josie (Medina) and Autumn in various ways," Williams is quoted as saying in a court transcript.

Williams faces a possible total maximum sentence on the two counts of seven years and fines of $500,000. Assistant U.S. Attorney Paul Engelmayer told the court that Williams had agreed to cooperate with authorities and if he is helpful prosecutors will recommend a lighter sentence.
He was released on a $250,000 personal recognisance bond.
His girlfriend Jackson returned to California on Monday to stay with her grandmother with whom she must remain under conditions of her bail.
She was released after two co-signers agreed to pay the $250,000 bond if she should flee. Jackson did not have to post any of the money.
Jackson and Medina, 51, were arrested ten days ago on extortion charges. He remains in federal prison.
In a portion of an interview shown on Monday night on the CBS Evening News, Cosby admitted to having "a rendezvous' with the girl's mother but denied being her father.
The entertainer's wife, Camille Cosby, made clear in a statement issued on Tuesday by Cosby's publicist that the affair was an old issue that had long been resolved.
According to court papers, Jackson was one of many young people for whom Cosby paid educational expenses for several years.
Federal prosecutors have said there was no evidence the scheme was connected to the murder of Cosby's son Ennis, killed by a gunman in Los Angeles on Jan 16.
